goal: Create an inference engine specially made for MiniCPM5 (debug using the debugging model: https://huggingface.co/tiny-random/minicpm5). The inference engine must end up as a cli with this usage: `tinyminigo -m model.safetensors --template chat_template.jinja  "What is the capital of France?"` and outputs everything the model returned. Use Rust.
refinedGoal: Build "TinyMiniGo": a from-scratch Rust CLI inference engine for MiniCPM5 (which uses the standard LlamaForCausalLM architecture: RMSNorm, GQA attention with RoPE, SwiGLU MLP). Correctness is validated against the tiny debug model https://huggingface.co/tiny-random/minicpm5 (hidden_size=16, 2 layers, 16 Q heads / 2 KV heads, head_dim=32, vocab 130560, SentencePiece tokenizer, Jinja chat template). Final deliverable: `tinyminigo -m model.safetensors --template chat_template.jinja "What is the capital of France?"` prints the model's full generated output. Helper crates allowed (safetensors, tokenizers, minijinja, clap); all inference math hand-rolled in pure Rust.

tasks.contract: Create a Rust binary crate `tinyminigo` in the repo root. Set up: clap-based CLI struct with exactly the required interface (-m <model.safetensors>, --template <chat_template.jinja>, positional PROMPT, plus optional --tokenizer <path>, --max-tokens N (default 256), --temperature, --top-k, --top-p, --repetition-penalty, --seed). Implement safetensors file parsing (header JSON + tensor offsets, mmap or read) exposing named tensors with dtypes (F32/BF16/F16). Implement tokenizer loading via the `tokenizers` crate (tokenizer.json), and chat-template rendering via `minijinja` using the provided .jinja file (last-message add_generation_prompt style, matching MiniCPM5's template). Provide stub functions for model loading & generation so the CLI end-to-end skeleton compiles and runs. `cargo build` must succeed.

tasks.contract: Implement model loading: parse config values needed (hidden_size, num_hidden_layers, num_attention_heads, num_key_value_heads, head_dim, intermediate_size, rms_norm_eps, rope_theta, vocab_size, eos_token_id) with sensible defaults when absent; map LlamaForCausalLM safetensors names (model.embed_tokens.weight, model.layers.N.self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj.weight, model.layers.N.mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight, model.layers.N.{input,post_attention}_layernorm.weight, model.norm.weight, lm_head.weight, handling tied embeddings when lm_head absent). result:
Built TinyMiniGo, a from-scratch Rust CLI inference engine for MiniCPM5 (LlamaForCausalLM architecture), validated numerically against the tiny-random/minicpm5 debug model.

Delivered:
- CLI exactly per spec: `tinyminigo -m model.safetensors --template chat_template.jinja "What is the capital of France?"` prints the model's full generated output (plus optional --tokenizer, --max-tokens, --temperature, --top-k, --top-p, --repetition-penalty, --seed flags).
- Pure-Rust inference math (src/tensor.rs): matmul (HF xW^T convention), RMSNorm, RoPE (HF rotate_half layout), SwiGLU, softmax, SDPA, sampling (greedy/temperature/top-k/top-p/repetition penalty, seeded).
- Model implementation (src/model.rs, src/config.rs): config parsing (incl. rope_parameters.rope_theta, list-valued eos_token_id), safetensors weight mapping with tied-embedding fallback, per-timestep GQA KV cache, prefill + incremental decode with EOS stopping.
- Chat templating (src/template.rs) via minijinja + minijinja-contrib pycompat so HF templates using Python string methods (startswith, lstrip, split, ...) render correctly.
- Robust CLI errors for missing model/template/tokenizer; deterministic greedy output.

Verification:
- 25 unit tests + 26 integration tests pass; clippy clean.
- Numerical cross-checks against Python transformers (scripts/hf_reference.py, hf_single_token.py, hf_layer_debug.py): first-step logits match to ~1e-6 (top-5 ids identical), layer-0 attention output matches <1e-3, and a 40-step greedy generation matches the HF reference character-for-character.
- Two bugs were found and fixed via the cross-check: RoPE layout (interleaved -> HF rotate_half) and KV-cache indexing (was treating KV heads as timesteps).
- README documents build, model download, usage, flags, and architecture.
